title: CmdPal: Stop reloading clipboard entries that haven't changed

proposed_comments.title: Preserve text-first clipboard format precedence
proposed_comments.body:
Please keep the established text-first precedence when a clipboard item exposes both text and an image. The current logic loads the bitmap before checking whether text is already present, so entries that contain both formats switch from text presentation/handling to image handling for the rest of the refresh flow. Guard the bitmap path behind `text == null` (or equivalent) so the optimization does not change the existing format precedence.

**Severity:** medium

confidence.rationale: The live code still prefers the bitmap branch before confirming text availability, while the converged fork fix leaves the original text-first ordering intact and was accepted by the follow-up review loop.

proposed_comments.title: Drain the cache before teardown and suppress stale refresh status
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ext/Microsoft.CmdPal.Ext.ClipboardHistory/Helpers/ClipboardHistorySource.cs` and `ClipboardHistorySource`; `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/ListViewModel.cs` and `ListViewModel`.

**Problem:** A queued refresh can race teardown, re-enter `ReadAsync` after disposal, and publish stale failure status after a newer refresh succeeds. The current implementation disposes `_source` before draining `_cache` and reports the failure even when a newer refresh has already won.

**Why it matters:** During page teardown, this can surface an `ObjectDisposedException` and leave the user with a bogus “failed to load” status even though the current refresh is no longer the active one.

**Suggested change:**
- Drain `_cache` before disposing `_source` so teardown cannot re-enter an already-disposed source.
- Guard the status/logging path behind the still-current refresh check so superseded or disposed work does not report a stale failure.
- Re-run the clipboard-history and view-model tests against the live head to confirm the refresh completes cleanly during teardown.

**Verification:** Confirm the refresh completes without `ObjectDisposedException` during teardown and that a superseded refresh no longer pushes a stale failure notification after a newer refresh succeeds.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The required sequencing spans the asynchronous cache and source lifetime, and the stale-refresh guard is split between the current-refresh check and the user-visible status/logging path; this is best expressed as one exact review prompt instead of several disconnected general findings.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The required sequencing spans the asynchronous cache and source lifetime, and the stale-refresh guard is split between the current-refresh check and the user-visible status/logging path; this is best expressed as one exact review prompt instead of several disconnected general findings.

confidence.rationale: The live logic still disposes the source before the cache and reports every exception, while the converged fork fix preserves the cache teardown ordering and conditions the user-visible failure report on the still-observed refresh.
